Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
It's a great card but you can't really rely on it:
- the first player who plays it win
- to take advantage of it (in matter of pool gain), you need to play Villein first (or Minion Tap)

If all 5 players have a Giant's Blood in their deck, it will be a dead card for 4 of them.

But feel free to build decks with 10 Giant's Blood in them if you want

Messages.Author: Kiddo
Messages.Body:
I stopped playing with Giant's Blood - there are too many conditions to be met to have it worthwhile being played AND there is such a high chance of contesting the use of it in tournament environment that I'd rather just spend my master slot on something I'll use whenever it comes and regardless of what other players are playing.

Far from it that GB is a bad card, it certainly isn't, but it is for me very far from auto-include when i build my decks, even with fatties...

Messages.Author: Izaak

Giant's Blood is ridiculously good.

It was quite playable before Villein, after Villein it's almost a must-include if only -as Ashur pointed out- to prevent someone else from getting a free 10-cap.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
> Izaak wrote:
> Giant's Blood is ridiculously good.
>
You stretch the definition of ridiculously good.

One time out of ten game, it will be extremely good. THe other nine game, another one will have played it first, or you will have played to gain 2-4 blood to make sure nobody beat you to it.

In any case, one thing you will surely agree upon is that you can't base strategy upon Giant Blood. You put it into your deck because it's almost alway a good thing to have, but it's not strategy-defining like Govern can be, or even a solid support like bleed redirection or Freak Drive. It's the lottery card that give you a solid advantage one game out of ten.

That depends on your definition of ridiculously good. Or even good. It fits mine just fine, but then again I´m all for banning it because of the stupid lottery aspect.

The problem with Giant's Blood is that it's not a concious deck construction decision whether or not you play it. You play it by default unless you specifically decide not to. And even then, your deck probably would be better with a copy in there.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
> Izaak wrote:
> I´m all for banning it because of the stupid lottery aspect.
>
> The problem with Giant's Blood is that it's not a concious deck construction decision whether or not you play it. You play it by default unless you specifically decide not to. And even then, your deck probably would be better with a copy in there.
>
I agree wholeheartedly with the lottery aspect and the fact it's not a conscious deck construction decision. It take only one slot, it's almost alway worth the master action, and you will almost never choke on it.

Where I beg to differ is that it is very good. Is a deck changed by removing the giant blood from it ? usually not. It will be a bit less good and won't have a chance to suddenly gain lot of blood, but it will still be playable and keep the same ability to gain victory point.

I am personnaly against the ban, but only because ban or errata are for disruptive card. I don't think the effect of Giant Blood is powerful enough to warrant such a drastic mesure.
